summary.headline: S H Kelkar Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA Rs 83 crore at 13.5% margin, steady sequentially; management guides ~13.5% for H1 FY27 despite raw-material inflation.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA was Rs 83 crore at a 13.5% margin, flat sequentially, after a one-off sale of about Rs 35 crore of low-margin products. FY26 reported EBITDA margin was 10.2%, with PAT hit by a higher consolidated tax rate from loss-making subsidiaries. Management said raw-material inflation (inventory prices up 12-13%+) had not yet hit Q4 but will show in coming quarters, and it is pricing through to clients on a 2-3 month inventory cycle. FY27 capex is guided at about Rs 140 crore and borrowings at about Rs 800 crore, with a full-year guidance withheld due to uncertainty.

FX contribution to revenue growth (Q4 and FY26)

financial_highlights.change: From Rs 93 crore in Q3; includes about Rs 6 crore one-off MTM impact in trust; normal run-rate Rs 94-95 crore per quarter
Equivalent to about Rs 50 crore annual business

segments.name: India Fragrance and Flavours (mature)
segments.commentary: Management put the mature India fragrance and flavours base at about Rs 1,300-1,400 crore, with flavours volumes growing rapidly and margins improving on operating leverage. India volumes dipped slightly in March due to Middle East shipment delays, since restored.

segments.name: Aroma Global Ingredients / Middle East / Southeast Asia
segments.commentary: Management called Middle East and Southeast Asia phase 2 growth markets. Q4 rest-of-world sales grew about 34% YoY per analyst question; Southeast Asia factory built last year with break-even reported.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Growth was muted over recent quarters because of capacity constraints. The Almere, Netherlands plant is now fully operational, with about Rs 10 crore of annual sales transferred on day one; management targets a return to double-digit growth.

segments.name: US and UK development centres
segments.commentary: US centre started last year and Manchester UK centre started this year. Management said US business of about 1 million (about 200,000 already in hand) is contracted; these are seen as 3-4 year ramps, with Rs 80-85 crore annual opex across three new centres.

guidance_outlook: Management expects to maintain adjusted EBITDA at about 13% to 13.5% through H1 FY27, with Q1 more visible and Q2 subject to monitoring; it wants to keep EBITDA above 12-13%.
Gross margin expected at about 42% and thereabouts in H1 FY27, with absolute profitability to be protected via pricing pass-through.
Management said it is confident of achieving Rs 300 crore-plus EBITDA in FY27 and at least FY25 levels, with more visibility on H1.
FY27 capex is expected at about Rs 140 crore, mostly front-loaded in the first two quarters.
Borrowings expected around Rs 800 crore in FY27; gross debt may rise in the next 3-6 months before falling, with a target to reduce debt by 10% every year over the long term.
Management declined to give full-year FY27 guidance, citing raw-material and inflation uncertainty beyond H1.
capex_capacity: Almere greenfield factory in Netherlands is fully operational, debottlenecking European growth that was near full utilisation.
Vanavate facility in Maharashtra expected to go on stream in coming months, likely around end of current quarter, with a six-month transition from the Mulund factory; Mulund to close next year.
Vashivali facility rebuild restarted after a fire; it may be available around Q3 FY27 but may not be needed immediately, with full operation next year.
Creative development centres in Germany (labs functional for a couple of months), Manchester UK, and US are the new opex-heavy initiatives, with break-even in about 3 years.
demand_pricing: Raw-material inventory prices are up about 12-13%+; power and fuel costs are also rising. About 40% of raw materials are directly crude-linked and about 30% indirectly linked.
Management said price increases have been secured from many clients, including large global accounts, and Q1 FY27 is described as secured on price, supply contracts and inventory.
Management expects overall industry demand to be muted in the next year or so, with share gains expected for the company during inflationary periods.
Management said it gained market share in India in the first few weeks of Q4-end, as smaller players hold less inventory buffer.
Flavours margins improved sequentially on rapid volume growth and operating leverage, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Return on the Rs 350 crore capex and Rs 80-85 crore opex in new centres: when will returns come?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said returns will take longer than 1-2 years; new centres break even after about 3 years and markets are 20-25x India in size. Management said it is on track in US and Europe and has no large India capex planned apart from fire-related rebuild.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins normalise to low teens this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, it expects to reach that level quickly, while noting the adjusted EBITDA target is about 13-13.5% for H1.

qa_highlights.question: How much raw material cost is passed on, and how will inventory cycles affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can pass on RM increases under contracts, holds 2-3 months of raw material and sets client prices against stock on hand, reviewing every 2-3 months; it expects no repeat of the past inventory-driven margin lag.

qa_highlights.question: FX impact on revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: FX added about 3% to 3.5% to revenue growth in Q4 and FY26; management said revenue transactions are broadly neutral but the dollar loan creates translation pressure on margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the detailed margin roadmap (13% to 17%) not been published, and what is the CCC outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the reported EBITDA target of about 14% by FY29 stands, but priorities have shifted to quarterly delivery after the March 2026 environment change. Cash conversion cycle is about 140 days and expected to persist until inflation stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Rs 35 crore low-margin exit hurt FY27 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no, citing strong demand and early indications in the first 45 days of Q1; European growth is expected to accelerate with the Almere plant.

risks_watch: Raw-material and crude-linked cost inflation has not yet fully flowed through; management expects pressure in coming quarters despite pricing actions.
Gross debt is expected to rise in the next 3-6 months due to inventory build, and insurance receipts after the fire may lag capex.
Start-up losses of about Rs 80-85 crore a year from US, UK and Germany development centres continue until revenue ramps (about 3 years).
Supplier contract honouring in flavours and raw material availability over the next 2-3 months.
Management did not give full-year FY27 guidance and deferred the detailed margin roadmap.
summary.management_tone: Confident on H1 FY27 margin and pricing visibility, but cautious and non-committal beyond H1 due to raw-material and inflation uncertainty. Management was candid about the Rs 35 crore one-off and the reported margin gap, and it deferred the detailed three-year margin plan.
key_quotes: So, as we have given our guidance and even if you look at the fourth quarter this year, we are at 13% and something adjusted EBITDA from the sustainable operating business.
We believe that we have taken adequate steps to keep close to this number at least for the first half of this year and we will wait and watch and see and take corrective steps as necessary.
Our key objective remains clear, protecting margins while ensuring supply security for our customers.
I am actually confident that we will hit the Rs. 300 crore plus EBITDA for this year.

growth.why: Management guides adjusted EBITDA margin ~13% in H1 FY27 and FY27 EBITDA of Rs 300 crore-plus, but declines full-year revenue guidance; FY27 capex of Rs 140 crore is front-loaded, and price pass-through and Vanavate/Vashivali capacity are cited, though revenue growth is not quantified.
